answer.line: Same metal both sides, so the standard potential is 0. The 100-fold gap makes the voltage: (0.0592 / 2) x log 100 = 0.059 V.

steps: Spot the setup: copper in both beakers. A concentration cell starts from a standard potential of 0.
Ask which way it runs. Cu^2+ plates out on the concentrated side, and the dilute side dissolves to catch up. A running cell reads positive.

choices.note: 0.0592 x 2 = 0.118 leaves out n. Cu^2+ takes two electrons, so the 0.0592 is halved first.
Flipping the ratio to 0.01 / 1.0 makes the dilute side the cathode. Copper plates out where Cu^2+ is concentrated, so the cell reads positive.
0 is the standard potential of a concentration cell. The concentrations differ 100 times, so the cell still makes a voltage.
0.0592 / 2 = 0.030 stops before multiplying by log 100, which is 2.

lockIt: A concentration cell has zero standard potential; its voltage is (0.0592 / n) log(concentrated / dilute).
